content:
Here is the mistake I see every week: a student turns a 7% rise into a base of 1.7 instead of 1.07. One misplaced digit and the money answer is wildly off. The whole topic hinges on one clean move, turning a percent into a multiplier. This free SAT Math Exponential Growth and Decay practice test drills that move until it is second nature. Fifteen Digital SAT-style MCQs sit below.

The base tells you everything

Every model looks like y = a×b^t. Here a is the start and b is the factor per step. So the base alone decides growth or decay. A base above 1 grows, and a base below 1 shrinks. Read b first, then the story makes sense.

  • A base of 1.20 means growth of 20% each period.
  • A base of 0.85 means decay of 15% each period.
  • Doubling uses a base of 2; halving uses a base of one-half.
  • The exponent counts how many periods have passed.

Percent to factor, the core of this SAT Math Exponential Growth and Decay practice test

This one conversion earns the most marks. So build it slowly, then speed up. For a rise, add the percent to 1. For a fall, subtract it from 1. A 7% gain is ×1.07, and a 7% loss is ×0.93. Simple, yet it decides nearly every item here.

The story saysThe factor bBehaviour
Up 15% a year1.15Growth
Down 15% a year0.85Decay
Triples each cycle3Fast growth
Loses half each cycle0.5Half-life decay

Growth is not linear

Students often add the same amount each year, but exponential change multiplies. So a town at 2000 growing 20% yearly reaches 2000×1.2² = 2880 after two years, not 2800. The gap looks small at first, yet it widens fast. That widening is exactly what the SAT probes.

A worked decay example

A car worth 25000 loses 15% of its value each year. So the factor is 0.85, and after three years the value is 25000×0.85³. That gives 25000×0.614125 = 15353.13. Notice you never subtracted 15% three separate times. One factor, raised to a power, does all the work. This is exactly why decay feels slow at first, then stubborn. Each year strips 15% of a smaller amount, so the drops shrink as you go. Trust the single factor, and let the exponent handle the years for you.

Reading the rate back out

Sometimes the SAT hands you the model and wants the rate. If P(t) = 500×1.08^t, then 1 + r = 1.08, so r = 0.08, which is 8% per hour. Flip the conversion and read the percent straight off the base. This reverse skill appears across the SAT Math Exponential Growth and Decay practice test.

Doubling time and half-life

Two phrases carry real weight here. Doubling time is how long a quantity takes to double, and half-life is how long it takes to halve. So a colony that doubles every 4 hours uses the exponent t divided by 4, with a base of 2. A sample that halves every 6 years uses t over 6, with a base of one-half. Match the period to the exponent and the model stays honest. Students often force the base to 2 while the timing hides in the exponent. So keep the two jobs separate: the base sets the direction, and the exponent counts the cycles. The SAT leans on this pairing in nearly every decay story.

questions.q: The model y = 800 · (1.2)^t describes which behavior?
questions.explanation: A base of 1.2 means the quantity gains 20% each period.

questions.q: A quantity grows by 15% each year. Which expression models its value after t years, starting from a?
questions.explanation: A 15% increase per year multiplies by 1.15 each year: value = a(1.15)^t. The linear option a + 15t changes by the same AMOUNT, not the same percent.

questions.q: A quantity starts at 2400 and increases 50% per period. What is its value after 2 periods?
A town of 2000 people grows 20% per year. What is the population after 2 years?
10000 is invested at 10% compounded annually. What is the amount after 2 years, in dollars?

A population of bacteria grows according to the function P(t) = 500(1.08)^t, where P(t) is the population after t hours. Which of the following best describes the hourly growth rate of the bacteria population?
questions.explanation: The function is in the form P(t) = a(1+r)^t. Here, 1+r = 1.08, so r = 0.08. Converting the decimal to a percentage, 0.08 × 100% = 8%.

questions.q: If 3ˣ⁺² = 9ˣ⁻¹, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Rewrite the equation with a common base: 3ˣ⁺² = (3²)ˣ⁻¹. Thus, 3ˣ⁺² = 3²ˣ⁻². Equating the exponents: x+2 = 2x-2. Solving for x, x=4.

questions.q: The model y = 800 · (1.15)^t describes which behavior?
questions.explanation: A base of 1.15 means the quantity gains 15% each period.

questions.q: A quantity starts at 2000 and increases 10% per period. What is its value after 2 periods?
A town of 12000 people grows 10% per year. What is the population after 2 years?
7000 is invested at 10% compounded annually. What is the amount after 2 years, in dollars?
The value of a car depreciates according to the function V(t) = 25000(0.85)^t, where V(t) is the value in dollars and t is the age of the car in years. What is the value of the car after 3 years?
Which of the following functions grows at the fastest rate for all x > 0?
questions.explanation: For exponential functions of the form f(x) = bˣ with b > 1, the function with the largest base b grows the fastest.

questions.q: The model y = 800 · (1.25)^t describes which behavior?
questions.explanation: A base of 1.25 means the quantity gains 25% each period.

questions.q: A quantity starts at 800 and increases 20% per period. What is its value after 2 periods?

faq.a: Yes. The 15 questions, the instant scoring and every worked step are free. The e-book then adds 100 more solved MCQs.

faq.q: How do I turn a percent into a growth factor?
faq.a: Add a rise to 1 and subtract a fall from 1. So +7% becomes ×1.07 and −7% becomes ×0.93. That single step drives the whole topic.

faq.q: How do I tell growth from decay?
faq.a: Read the base b in y = a×b^t. A base above 1 means growth, and a base below 1 means decay. Nothing else matters for that call.

faq.q: Why is exponential growth not the same as adding a percent?
faq.a: Each period multiplies the previous total, so the increase itself keeps growing. Adding a fixed amount is linear, and the two answers split apart fast.
